title: On septic in Sebastian? Who runs your sewer, the hookup grant, and where the projects stand
seoTitle: Sebastian Septic to Sewer: Grant, Projects, 2030 Rule
description: Sebastian homes on septic: the county runs sewer here, who must connect by 2030, the up-to-$15,000 hookup grant, and North Sebastian Phase 3 news.
dek: Sebastian is inside the lagoon basin covered by Florida's 2030 septic rule, and the city has no sewer utility of its own. Here is who to call, who can get help paying to hook up, and what is happening in Sebastian neighborhoods.
keywords: Indian River County sewer connection grant

body.text: A lot of Sebastian homes still run on septic tanks. If yours does, the last few weeks may have been confusing. Indian River County planned a set of septic-to-sewer workshops, held two in Vero Beach, then canceled the rest, including both sessions at the North County Library on Sebastian Boulevard.
The county has now changed how it is reaching people. This is a good time to sort out what the rules say, who is in charge in Sebastian, and whether your house can get help paying for a hookup.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Sebastian does not run its own sewer system. Sewer here comes from Indian River County. Under a 2023 state law, septic homes in the lagoon basin must connect to sewer where it is available, or switch to a nitrogen-reducing septic system, by July 1, 2030. Sebastian is inside that basin.

The City of Sebastian does not operate a sewer utility. It relies on Indian River County's Department of Utility Services. Some Sebastian neighborhoods have no sewer main in the street at all. In those areas, hooking up is not as simple as paying a fee, because the pipe is not there yet.

So for septic and sewer questions, the county is the place to start. The county's septic-to-sewer program can be reached by email at projectinfo@IRCS2SProgram.com, and project details are posted at ircs2sprogram.com.

The state law was passed in 2023. It covers homes on conventional septic systems inside the Central Indian River Lagoon basin, which includes Sebastian. About 28,000 properties in Indian River County fall under it, according to Sebastian Daily.

By July 1, 2030, those properties must either connect to central sewer or replace the tank with an enhanced system that cuts nitrogen by at least 65%. County Utilities Director Sean Lieske put it plainly to WQCS: "If sewer is available, the State law requires property owners to connect to central sewer." The canceled workshops did not change the deadline.
The hookup grant, and who can get it now

The county's Sewer Connection Assistance Program offers up to $15,000 per eligible property, paid with Florida Department of Environmental Protection grant money. It is for properties where sewer is already available. Aid is based on income and is first come, first served. The county's program site says the application portal has not opened yet.

A property counts as able to connect now if it sits within 100 feet of a gravity sewer line, or of a force main smaller than 6 inches. The county estimates about 463 properties countywide fit that test, and says the real number may be a bit lower.

To reach those owners, the county plans a second letter after its first mailing, an automated phone call, and email where it has addresses. Smaller meetings about eligibility are planned. Even with the grant, owners may still pay thousands of dollars to run a line from the house to the street and close out the old tank, Sebastian Daily reported.
What is happening in Sebastian neighborhoods

items: North Sebastian Phase 3: 168 homes on roads around the North Sebastian area. Engineering and design are underway, and the county held a community meeting on June 17, 2026.

The CRA district and waterfront: in April 2025, Sebastian and the county approved an agreement to extend county sewer into the city's Community Redevelopment Area. About 96 properties on septic would be able to connect. The city pledged up to $100,000 for materials, and staff said an ordinance requiring connection would be proposed.
A citywide look: in November 2025, county commissioners approved a feasibility study of septic-to-sewer conversion for Sebastian. It is set to compare gravity, low-pressure and vacuum sewer systems.

body.text: In county projects, the county puts the main line in the street and runs a lateral pipe to each property. The homeowner pays for the final connection from the house to that lateral. "We don't manage anything that's on private property," Lieske told WQCS. He urged owners to use a licensed, bonded plumber, especially for gravity connections, where getting the slope right matters.

County leaders say the costs are hard on residents. The county has asked the state for about $50 million for connections, and commissioners plan to push for more state money in the 2027 legislative session.

items: Confirm whether your home is on septic or sewer. Your home's records or the county's utility office can tell you.
Open your mail and answer the phone. If the county sends a letter or calls about connecting, your home may be one of the properties that can connect now and apply for aid.
Email projectinfo@IRCS2SProgram.com to ask whether sewer is available at your address and whether your street is in a planned project.
If you live in the North Sebastian Phase 3 area or the CRA district, watch for project notices and meeting dates.
If you will need to connect, get quotes from licensed plumbers before the rush. You can check a license at myfloridalicense.com.
Keep up normal septic care in the meantime. A failing tank is a problem long before 2030.

faq.a: No. The City of Sebastian does not run a sewer utility. Sewer service in Sebastian comes from Indian River County, and some neighborhoods do not have a sewer main yet.

faq.q: Do I have to connect to sewer in Sebastian by 2030?
faq.a: Sebastian is inside the Central Indian River Lagoon basin. Under a 2023 state law, homes on conventional septic there must connect to sewer where it is available, or switch to an enhanced nitrogen-reducing septic system, by July 1, 2030.

faq.q: Is there a grant to connect to sewer in Indian River County?
faq.a: Yes. The county's Sewer Connection Assistance Program offers up to $15,000 per eligible property where sewer is already available. It is income-based and first come, first served. The county says the application portal has not opened yet.

faq.q: When will North Sebastian Phase 3 get sewer?
faq.a: The project covers 168 homes and is in engineering and design. The county has not posted a construction date on its program site. Email projectinfo@IRCS2SProgram.com for updates.
